newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: GOLF-OLAZABAL WITHIN SIGHT OF COMEBACK VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-OLAZABAL WITHIN SIGHT OF COMEBACK VICTORY.

text.p: Jose Maria Olazabal moved to within sight of a remarkable comeback victory when he produced a brilliant third round 65 in the Portuguese Open on Saturday.

The former U.S. Masters champion swept into a share of second place with Paul Broadhurst on a 14-under-par total of 202, just two strokes behind little-known Swede Michael Jonzon with whom he will play in Sunday's final round.
Jonzon, who has yet to win a European event, shot 68 for 200, birdying the 18th to retain the advantage he held over the field at the halfway mark.
Broadhurst, Olazabal's team mate in the 1991 Ryder Cup team, hit 67 but Australians Wayne Riley and Peter O'Malley both struggled after poor starts.
Riley was joined in a share of fourth place on 205 by Mark Davis and Van Phillips, both of England.
Olazabal was still cautious despite his brilliant form.
"I was testing myself in Dubai and I am still testing myself here," the Spaniard said.

"So far things are going my way but I was lucky because I pulled four shots towards trees and each time found a good lie from where I could reach the green. I am not fully sharp yet but I admit things are going much better than I could have hoped to expect."
Jonzon said: "It was a good day's work and I felt good. This is a new experience for me and everyone knows that Olazabal is a great competitor under pressure. I will just try to stay ahead of him."
